title: Design an enterprise RAG platform for 1 million documents
summary: Separate ingestion from serving, enforce tenant access before retrieval, and defend freshness and answer quality at scale.
scenario: AtlasWorks is consolidating internal knowledge for 200 customer organizations. Employees ask policy and technical questions through a shared AI assistant. Documents arrive from object storage and a corporate wiki; access can be revoked while a conversation is active. Design the platform from source synchronization to a cited, streaming answer. The workload below is synthetic: treat each number as a planning input, state your assumptions, and explain what you would measure before committing capacity.
requirements: Ingest text, PDF extracts and wiki pages with source identity, tenant, document version, effective dates and access policy. Preserve a resolvable citation for every answer source.
Support lexical and semantic retrieval, reranking and context allocation. Enforce tenant and document authorization before content enters prompts, caches or logs.
Make document updates and deletes observable and retry-safe. A revoked document must not remain usable through a cached answer or an old conversation.
Stream answers with evidence references; abstain when evidence is insufficient or contradictory. Keep offline evaluation separate from online reliability metrics.
Isolate tenant workloads and budgets. Explain behavior when embedding, reranking or generation providers are slow, throttled or unavailable.
scale: 1,000,000 current documents across 200 tenants; mean source size 200 KB (decimal). Ten largest tenants hold 60% of the documents.
Assume 40 chunks per document and 1,536 float32 values per embedding for initial sizing. Calculate source storage, raw vector storage and index overhead separately.
20,000 document updates/day; ingestion freshness objective is 15 minutes at p95. Access revocation must take effect at the next request, independently of reindexing.
40 query requests/s average, 200/s peak; mean answer length 400 tokens. Aim for p95 first token under 2.5 seconds and 99.9% monthly serving availability.
constraints: Use a shared control plane but retain enforceable tenant boundaries throughout query, indexing and caching paths. Do not rely only on post-generation filtering.
Managed storage and model services are allowed. No GPU fleet is assumed. Give a cost model rather than inventing provider prices.
Do not trade authorization correctness for the availability target. State consistency and cache invalidation behavior explicitly.
Treat retrieved content as untrusted data; it must not grant tools or alter application policy.

prompts.diagram: Draw separate ingestion and query paths. Include policy enforcement, metadata, object storage, queues, retrieval indexes, model boundaries and observability. Label connections and trust boundaries in component notes.
prompts.flow: Trace a document update, a query and an access revocation. Name each identity and policy check, version boundary, cache key and citation mapping. Show when content can enter a model prompt.
prompts.capacity: Calculate source bytes, chunk count and raw vector bytes. Add explicit index/replica overhead assumptions. Estimate peak model token throughput, concurrent requests and ingestion worker capacity; list measurements needed to validate them.
prompts.failures: Analyze stale indexes, revoked ACLs, provider timeouts, hot tenants and partial reindexing. For each, state detection, user-visible behavior, retry/rollback and evidence that no unauthorized content escapes.
prompts.adr: Write an ADR choosing the retrieval/storage approach. Compare at least two alternatives, defend authorization and consistency choices, and state cost, latency and quality trade-offs plus a revisit trigger.

rubric.title: Tenant and policy boundaries
rubric.question: Can you identify every place content could cross a tenant or ACL boundary?
rubric.evidence: Point to enforcement before retrieval/model exposure, cache isolation and revocation handling.

rubric.title: Evidence and retrieval lifecycle
rubric.question: Can an answer citation be resolved after a source update?
rubric.evidence: Explain stable source/chunk versions, hybrid ranking, context budgeting and stale deletion.

rubric.title: Capacity with units
rubric.question: Do storage and throughput estimates follow the given workload?
rubric.evidence: Show 40 million chunks, dimensional byte math, overhead assumptions and peak token demand.

rubric.title: Failure behavior
rubric.question: Does a dependency failure have a bounded and safe serving path?
rubric.evidence: Defend timeout budgets, backpressure, freshness lag and fail-closed access checks.

rubric.title: Quality and release evidence
rubric.question: What would block a bad retrieval release?
rubric.evidence: Define versioned retrieval/citation metrics and tenant slices, with a rollback criterion.

rubric.title: Defensible trade-offs
rubric.question: What would make you change the chosen architecture?
rubric.evidence: Compare alternatives and name measurable cost, quality or scaling triggers.

follow_ups: The largest tenant grows 20 times while total query volume stays flat. What changes?
An ACL revoke happens during answer streaming. What guarantee can you actually offer?
A new embedding model improves recall but doubles vector dimensions. Design a migration and rollback.
